memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Isaac reopened the wells that had been dug in the time of his father Abraham, which the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham died, and he gave them the same names his father had given them." - Gen 26:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Rather than starting entirely from scratch, Isaac goes back and reopens the wells his father Abraham had dug — the ones the Philistines had filled with earth. And tenderly, he gives them the same names his father had given them. He is reclaiming a heritage that others had tried to bury.

There is something beautiful in this picture. Sometimes the way forward is to recover what was lost. The wells of faith that our parents or spiritual forebears once dug — habits of prayer, love for God's Word, family worship, honesty, generosity — can get "stopped up" over time, filled in by neglect, busyness, or the pressures of the world. Isaac reminds us that these springs can be reopened.

Is there a well in your own life that has been filled in? A prayer life that has dried up? A faith you once held with fresh joy? A godly practice you have let slip? You do not always need something brand new; sometimes you need to dig out the old, good things again and let the water flow.

Honour the faith that came before you by keeping its wells open. What blessed earlier generations can bless you too, if you are willing to clear away the earth and drink again.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What good spiritual "well" in my life has been filled in over time?
2. What faithful practice do I need to reopen and reclaim?
3. How can I honour the faith of those who came before me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to reopen the wells of faith that have been filled in — prayer, Your Word, and devotion to You. Let living water flow freshly in my life again. Amen.
